_about: End-of-career epilogue lines. Tokens: {J} {club} last club, {FIRSTCLUB} first club, {MUM} {DAD} {SIB} {SIBr} {BF} {BFf} {Pf} {RIVAL} {MENTEE} {OLDBOSS} {WEALTH} {KIDS}.

coach: {J} takes his coaching badges further and starts with an under-15 team. The kids complain he makes them run too much. Within five years he's an assistant at {club}.
He goes straight into coaching. His first team talk is a disaster. His second one is better. By forty he has his own dugout and the same intensity he had as a player.
pundit: Television snaps him up. He's honest, a bit too honest, and the clips of him criticising former teammates get millions of views.
{J} becomes a pundit: sharp suit, sharper opinions. The journalists he once dodged now share a studio with him.
foundation: The foundation becomes his life's work: pitches in villages, scholarships, a programme for kids who can't afford boots. He says it's the best thing he ever did, and he means it.
He runs his foundation full-time. Every year, a few more kids get the chance he almost didn't.
business: He invests in businesses back home: a futsal chain, a coffee brand, a property or two. Not all of it works. Enough of it does.
{J} becomes a businessman. He's better at it than anyone expected, possibly including himself.
broke: The money is gone. The debts are not. He takes a job coaching kids on weekends and selling insurance on weekdays, and he's quieter than anyone remembers.
Retirement starts with a bank meeting he'd rather forget. He sells the medals he can bear to part with. Some friends help. Not many.
shadow: The headlines follow him into retirement. Offers dry up. He moves somewhere quieter and tries to become someone else.
Nobody calls with jobs. His name still sells newspapers, just not in the way he'd like.
quiet: He chooses a quiet life: a house near the sea, a small pitch in the garden, an alarm clock he never sets again.
{J} disappears from public life almost completely. Sometimes he plays five-a-side with people who have no idea who he was.

high: {MUM} keeps every newspaper clipping in a cabinet in the living room. Visitors are made to look at all of them.
Sunday lunch at his parents' house becomes sacred. {DAD} finally admits, out loud, that he was proud of him all along.
mid: Family life settles into something comfortable: calls on Sundays, visits at holidays, old arguments that never quite get resolved.
He's closer to his family than he was in the hard years, if not as close as he'd like.
low: The distance from the playing years never fully closes. He calls home more than he used to. It isn't always answered.
His family are proud of the footballer. They're still getting to know the man.
oldParents: His father is old now, and {J} takes him to every match at {FIRSTCLUB}, where it all began.
lostDad: On the anniversary of {DAD}'s death every year, {J} goes back to {FIRSTCLUB} and kicks a ball against the wall where his father taught him to play.
A photo of {DAD} in the stands sits on his desk. He looks at it every morning.

marriedHappy: He and {Pf} grow old the way they promised: arguing about restaurants, holding hands on the sofa.
{Pf} and {J} are still together, still laughing at the same terrible films.
marriedStrained: The marriage survives, but the hard years left marks. They work at it. Some years are better than others.
He and {Pf} stay together, quieter than they used to be. Retirement gives them time to learn each other again.
together: He and {Pf} finally have the time they never had during his career. They spend it travelling, mostly to places without stadiums.
single: He never quite found the right person during the playing years. Retirement, he says, is his chance.
Single, and surprisingly at peace with it.
singleParent: He raises his children mostly on his own, at every school play, every grazed knee.
kids: {KIDS} grow up hearing stories about his career and pretending to be unimpressed.
{KIDS} have his old shirts framed in their rooms. One of them is already better at keepy-uppy than he ever was.

high: {BFf} is still his best friend: still {BFjob}, still roasting him in the group chat. Some things never change, and he's grateful.
The old crew still meet every month at the same cheap restaurant. Nobody lets him pay.
low: He realises, too late, how many friendships he let fade. He starts calling people again. Some of them pick up.

friend: {RIVAL}, the boy he once fought for a place, becomes his closest friend in football. They open a coaching school together.
{RIVAL} speaks at his testimonial dinner and makes the whole room cry with a story about the youth team.
enemy: He and {RIVAL} never speak again. When asked about each other, both say 'no comment' in exactly the same tone.
{RIVAL} still won't shake his hand at legends matches.
neutral: He sees {RIVAL} at a legends match years later. They nod, and that's enough.

star: The kid he helped, {MENTEE}, becomes a star. In his first big interview he thanks {J} by name.
{MENTEE}, the boy he once mentored, plays in front of eighty thousand people and dedicates his first goal to {J}.
normal: The kids he mentored send him messages on his birthday every year. One of them is now a coach himself.

kept: He kept his promise. The people of his hometown never forget it: there's a mural of {J} on the wall of the old stadium.
He went back, like he said he would. The final chapter at home is the one people talk about most.
broken: He never went back, despite the promise. In his hometown, his name gets a complicated silence.
The promise was broken. There's a banner at {FIRSTCLUB} that still says so.

high: The fans of {club} chant his name at the first home match after he retires. He's in the stand, and he can't stop crying.
There's talk of a statue. He laughs it off. They build it anyway.
mid: Fans remember him fondly, the way you remember a good season.
He gets a warm round of applause whenever he goes back to {club}.
low: The fans aren't sentimental about him. He'd hoped for more. Maybe he should have given them more.

rich: He retires with {WEALTH} and the strange problem of having more money than time. He gives a lot of it away.
Financially, he never has to work again. His mother still checks he's eating properly.
comfortable: He leaves the game comfortable: a paid-off house, savings, and a plan.
Money isn't a worry. That was never guaranteed, and he knows it.
modest: He retires with less than people assume. Footballers' money isn't what fans think. He gets a job, and he's fine.
The savings are modest. He's proud of every cent of them.
debt: He retires in debt. It takes years to pay back. He tells young players about it every chance he gets.

high: Parents still point him out to their children: 'That's how you do it.'
He's remembered as one of the good ones.
mid: He's remembered the way most players are: a few great moments, a few mistakes, a lot of hard work in between.
History is kind to him, mostly.
low: The controversies follow his name like a shadow. Some people remember the football. More remember the headlines.
